item.title: Google Discovers Botnet in Android Devices
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Digital Trends Original headline: Google Unveils Massive Botnet Infection in Android Devices
Google discovered a backdoor embedded in 1.3 million Android devices by Videostrong Technology Co., a manufacturing partner. The malware, built into firmware and activated during first boot, enabled unauthorized access for cybercrime activities including ad fraud, data exfiltration, and routing traffic. Videostrong monetized the botnet by selling access to criminal groups, who deployed additional malware to create proxy networks and infect IoT devices like telehealth equipment and digital signage. The malware persisted even after removal, reinstalling upon device restart. Google terminated its partnership with Videostrong, disrupted command-and-control servers, and collaborated with security firms and Japan’s National Police Agency to dismantle the botnet. The company revised certification processes and advised users to replace Videostrong-branded devices. Experts warn existing malware on infected devices may still pose risks unless replaced. Google emphasized actions to disrupt criminal networks could limit further exploitation of compromised hardware.

item.title: OpenAI Merges Chat and Work Tabs into Unified ChatGPT Experience
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: OpenAI is merging Chat and Work into one ChatGPT experience
OpenAI is merging the Chat and Work tabs into a single ChatGPT experience, allowing users to handle conversations and complex tasks in one interface. The change will initially roll out to select users before a wider release. Previously, ChatGPT had separate tabs for regular conversations and work-related tasks like research, presentations, and website building. The new setup lets users switch between tasks seamlessly, use files and plugins, and track projects without tab-switching. Codex, used for programming, remains a separate experience in the desktop app. Starting December, ChatGPT and Codex will share usage limits for Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers, though regular Instant chats won’t count toward the shared allowance. OpenAI hasn’t specified an exact date for the full rollout of the merged experience.

item.title: Hidden Nudifying Tools Found in AI Apps
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: A hidden network of nudifying tools was found lurking inside harmless looking AI apps
Hundreds of apps on Google Play and Apple App Store were found to hide deepfake generators disguised as harmless tools like pet portrait makers or workout coaches. Researchers from AI Forensics uncovered a network of 400+ connected apps and domains that switched to hidden interfaces under specific conditions, such as user location or ad-click triggers. These interfaces allowed users to generate explicit deepfakes using real photos, with some apps accepting payments via Apple Pay and Google Pay. The network, linked to Chinese developers and a Hong Kong entity called KeLing Technology Limited, spread through deceptive ads on Meta platforms. Apple and Google removed dozens of apps after investigations, including the pet portrait app Viefur. Meta banned KeLing in 2025 and took action against 11,600 ad accounts. The EU’s ban on nudifier apps takes effect soon, but similar ads continued to appear during the investigation.

item.title: European Supermarkets' Freezers Hacked, Spoiling Millions in Food
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, Gizmodo, The Verge - Cybersecurities, PCMag Original headline: European Supermarkets Hit by Cyberattacks That Turned Freezers Into Ovens
Supermarket freezers across Europe were hacked, raising temperatures to 50°C and spoiling millions in food. The attack affected dozens of stores in Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia, Finland, and Germany, including chains like Delhaize, Carrefour, and ICA. Managers reported losses exceeding €100,000, with one stating, 'Hot air is getting into the freezers. Everything is ruined.' Cybersecurity experts linked the breach to outdated Danfoss refrigeration software, previously exploited in French supermarkets. Patrick Lamplmair of Tributech warned, 'A freezer should never accept an instruction to heat to 50°C.' The attacks followed earlier U.S. military base intrusions, with the Pentagon reviewing incidents. EU Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen called the weaponization of food a 'reality,' urging stronger cybersecurity. Belgium, Sweden, and the UK are collaborating to assess the breach, with Sabcobel confirming hardware upgrades were needed. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in connected infrastructure, as experts warn basic systems like freezers can become critical targets.
item.source: Digital Trends, Gizmodo, The Verge - Cybersecurities, PCMag

item.title: Garmin Uses Nano Molding to Make Titanium Cases for Fenix 9 Pro and Marq Gen 3
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Garmin explains the process behind the Fenix 9 Pro and Marq Gen 3's new titanium case
Garmin uses titanium in the Fenix 9 Pro and Marq Gen 3 watches but faces technical hurdles. Titanium is lighter and stronger than aluminum or stainless steel, but all-metal cases block radio signals needed for Bluetooth, LTE, and GPS. Garmin COO Brad Trenkle explained that polymer parts are essential to maintain connectivity while keeping the watch lightweight. The solution involves 'nano molding,' a process that bonds polymer and titanium at the nano scale without gaskets. Todd Register, Garmin’s Creative lead, described how etching titanium allows a polymer to interlock with the metal, creating a tight bond. This method avoids the bulk of traditional gaskets, preventing the 'tuna can' feel of past models like the Forerunner 201. Nano molding was previously tested by HTC in 2011 but remains costly. Garmin’s Venu series could benefit from all-titanium casings, though price increases may deter buyers. The Marq Gen 3’s design prioritizes durability and comfort over style, balancing performance with wearability.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Anthropic Warns of AI's Recursive Self-Improvement Risks
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Gizmodo Original headline: Anthropic Warns of Looming Recursive Self-Improvement Risks in AI Development
Anthropic, the AI research lab behind Claude, warns in its S-1/A filing that its models may soon reach a critical threshold of recursive self-improvement (RSI), where AI systems could autonomously enhance their capabilities, accelerating progress dramatically. The filing acknowledges both risks of losing control and opportunities for scientific advancement. Anthropic emphasizes maintaining human oversight and outlines its Responsible Scaling Policy, including security protocols and oversight mechanisms. While current models have not crossed the RSI threshold, internal estimates suggest future models may meet the definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI.' The company notes that AI has already been used to develop models exceeding expectations, raising concerns about rapid escalation. Anthropic’s commitments include exploring 'unconventional security measures' and implementing 'eyes on everything' oversight, reducing reliance on external red-teaming. The filing highlights the growing debate around RSI’s implications for AI governance, underscoring the need for safeguards as capabilities advance rapidly.

item.title: Anthropic restricts Claude from cloning existing video games
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Gizmodo, Ars Technica, PCWorld Original headline: Anthropic Restricts Claude's Ability to Clone Existing Video Games
Anthropic updated Claude Code's system prompt to prevent the AI from recreating specific existing video games. The change, part of Opus 5.5, instructs Claude to focus on original games, genre-based projects, or user-generated designs, explicitly banning recreations of specific titles even if renamed. Addy Osmani, Anthropic's engineering leader, confirmed the update aligns with policies against intellectual property infringement. The move follows concerns about AI-assisted game cloning, which has led to increased decompilation and recreation of classic titles. A GitHub user documented the change in a file labeled 'tengu_heron_brook,' later verified in version 2.1.314 of the Claude Code binary released October 30. Some developers report the new prompt hinders legitimate use cases. Gizmodo noted potential loopholes, as the rule does not address recreations of non-existing games or IP franchises. PCWorld highlighted that reverse-engineering requires more than prompts, often involving decompiling ROMs, as seen in a 2021 lawsuit against Take Two Interactive. Despite restrictions, AI-driven game cloning continues, with tools emerging to recreate titles like Diablo II and The Legend of Zelda: Link to the Past.
item.source: The Verge, Gizmodo, Ars Technica, PCWorld

item.title: How long could HDDs and SSDs remain expensive?
item.description:
Source: Engadget
Hard disk drives (HDDs) and solid-state drives (SSDs) remain expensive due to ongoing chip shortages, though relief is expected. Prices for both storage types have been significantly higher than pre-pandemic levels, with HDDs offering cost-effective mass storage despite slower speeds compared to SSDs. Industry analysts predict a gradual price decline starting in 2027, with more noticeable drops likely by 2029 or 2030. While SSDs face flash memory shortages, HDDs are expected to retain value due to their durability and lower cost. Experts caution that full recovery to pre-COVID price levels may not occur, and consumers are advised to wait for sharper price reductions before purchasing storage solutions.

item.title: Apple AirPods chirp for reasons beyond low battery
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Your Apple AirPods' chirping noise doesn't just mean low battery
Apple AirPods emit chirping noises for reasons beyond low battery. The sounds may result from power fluctuations, connectivity issues, Bluetooth disconnection, or physical contact between earbuds. The Hearing Aid feature in AirPods Pro 2 and 3 can trigger periodic quiet chimes to test microphone and speaker performance. Louder noises occur when the Find My feature is activated, aiding in locating lost devices. Water damage, earwax buildup, or improper ear tip fit can also cause feedback or high-pitched sounds. Users can disable charging case sounds via Settings on their paired iPhone by turning off the 'Enable Charging Case Sounds' option. Apple recommends using provided silicone tips for a proper seal or seeking professional assistance for persistent issues.

item.title: Apple Tests AI Audio Features for Apple Watch
item.description:
Source: Engadget, TechCrunch Original headline: Apple Introduces AI-Powered Audio Features for Apple Watch in Beta Testing
Apple has begun beta testing two new Audio Intelligence features for its Apple Watch lineup: Siri Recap and Live Rewind. These features, part of watchOS 27.3, are available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 models. Siri Recap generates summaries of conversations with titles and key points, avoiding sensitive details. Live Rewind lets users review the last 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet by double-pressing the Digital Crown, with a chime and visual indicator. Both features require a compatible iPhone with Apple Intelligence enabled, such as an iPhone 16 or later, and are limited to English initially. Privacy safeguards include the S11 chip processing audio in isolation, preventing storage or access by apps, users, or Apple. Features like sound recognition for alarms and faster Shazam detection are also included. Apple clarified these tools do not record or store audio, and users can opt out of individual functions. Live Rewind and Siri Recap are opt-in, with some requiring manual activation. The features aim to assist in scenarios like meetings or parent-teacher conferences while addressing privacy concerns, such as not activating when using headphones or noise cancellation. This marks Apple’s expansion of AI-driven audio tools into its wearable ecosystem.

item.title: Cyclon launches AI phone that automates app tasks
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Cyclon wants to replace your iPhone with an AI phone that actually gets things done
Cyclon, a Y Combinator F26 startup, aims to replace traditional smartphones with an AI-driven device that automates routine tasks. Unlike existing assistants, Cyclon navigates apps independently, switching between them to complete tasks like sending photos from WhatsApp. It can also create temporary apps on demand and operates in the background. The company is launching its first devices as Pixel 8a phones with Cyclon preinstalled, shipping within 30 days of preorder. Custom hardware is planned for future models to run advanced AI models locally while keeping data on-device. However, reliability remains uncertain, as the AI must adapt to each app's unique interface. Success could reduce tedious manual tasks, but failure risks repeating the shortcomings of past assistants.

item.title: Germany Warns Lawmakers Over iPhone Spyware Threats
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Germany says lawmakers’ iPhones may have been hacked with spyware
Germany’s government warns lawmakers and public figures their iPhones may have been hacked with spyware. The federal cybersecurity office, BSI, confirmed members of the Bundestag and unnamed individuals received Apple notifications about potential cyberattacks. Apple sends threat alerts when it detects spyware, which can steal data via zero-click exploits. German spokesperson Stefan Kornelius emphasized the government takes the incident seriously but did not specify targeted officials, including Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Apple does not attribute attacks to specific governments or confirm compromises. The warnings reached users in 99 countries, including filmmaker Radwan Mortada, who previously faced a 2021 spyware attack. The incident underscores the use of mercenary spyware vendors like Israel’s NSO Group, which sells Pegasus. Germany’s BKA reportedly purchased Pegasus access in 2019, highlighting the role of private firms in state-sponsored cyber operations.

item.title: Readwise launches app challenging Kindle and Goodreads with detailed reading metrics
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Readwise takes on Amazon’s Kindle and Goodreads with its new app for book lovers
Readwise launched Readwise Books, an e-book store and reading tracker combining features of Kindle and Goodreads. The app allows users to buy, read, and track books with detailed metrics like words read, pace, depth, and immersion. It offers millions of e-books from major publishers, plus print and audiobooks, expanding to international markets. Readwise emphasizes open technology, including a public API and MCP server for AI agents that can generate recommendations, create personal book pages, or sync with e-readers. The app remains free, with some AI features planned for a paywall. Founders Daniel Doyon and Tristan Homsi compared the app to Strava, arguing that measurable reading sessions reduce guilt and improve habits. Unlike Kindle’s closed ecosystem, Readwise supports DRM-free EPUBs, text-to-speech, and photo-based progress tracking. The company claims users read more without relying on goal-setting or streaks. AI features like session recaps and definitions are available with publisher permission, starting with HarperCollins.

item.title: Apple's HomeView Could Add Indoor Security Camera Feature
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Apple HomeView May Soon Become an Indoor Security Camera
Apple's HomeView may soon offer indoor security camera functionality through HomeKit Secure Video, as revealed by code in the HomeView 27.2 update. The feature, not announced during the device's initial launch, allows users to access camera feeds via the Home app. Privacy controls include restricting viewing to household members, with visual and auditory alerts for recording or streaming. Code also mandates notifications for any changes to recording settings, preventing unauthorized adjustments. The Home app integrates with the LG Video Doorbell ($249.95), enabling users to switch between forward-facing and downward-facing camera views by swiping down. Apple has not confirmed if the security camera feature will debut at launch or require a future software update.

item.title: Study finds cognitive reappraisal measures disagree
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Most of our measures of a key cognitive process don't agree
A study published in Nature reveals that common methods for measuring cognitive reappraisal—a key process in cognitive behavioral therapy—do not consistently capture the same aspects of the ability. Researchers analyzed three widely used indices: trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings after reappraisal, and amygdala down-regulation during reappraisal. They found these measures fail to align, suggesting current tools cannot reliably assess the capacity for cognitive reappraisal. The findings challenge assumptions about how to evaluate this skill, which is central to therapies aimed at improving emotional resilience. The study highlights a gap in understanding how to effectively measure a process critical to CBT, potentially impacting how therapeutic outcomes are assessed. The researchers note that the lack of agreement among measures undermines efforts to standardize evaluations of reappraisal capacity, raising questions about the reliability of existing psychological assessments.

item.title: Ukraine's D·Vision SDR intercepts Russian drones' live video feeds
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Ukraine’s new pocket-sized gadget turns Russian drones’ cameras against them
Ukrainian startup CODE380 has developed the D·Vision SDR, a pocket-sized receiver that intercepts live video feeds from Russian drones. The device, weighing about 10 ounces, captures unscrambled camera signals transmitted by drones, allowing users to track their movements and targets in real time. It detects video from newer Molniya drones, which began using specific radio channels in June. Serhii "Flash" Beskrestnov, a Ukrainian radio specialist, warned that most existing detectors struggle with these frequencies, risking fatal consequences if relied upon. He also noted that digital video could replace analog signals, rendering current receivers ineffective. The New York Times reported that some Molniya drones use AI guidance with Nvidia chips and emit no signals, complicating detection efforts.

item.title: Two 256GB Mac Studios cheaper than one 512GB unit
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Apple charges over 100% more to double Mac Studio M5 Ultra memory, making two 256GB units cheaper than one 512GB
Apple's Mac Studio M5 Ultra 512GB configuration costs $22,299, while two 256GB units total $11,500. Critics argue purchasing two smaller systems provides more hardware for less money, as each includes separate CPUs, GPUs, and storage. The 512GB version uses specialized 8GB memory chips instead of the 4GB components in the 256GB model, contributing to the $11,500 price difference. Apple's technical explanation notes the M5 Ultra has 64 memory channels with varying chip capacities. Thunderbolt 5 allows connecting two units for data transfer but doesn't merge memory pools. Users can run separate AI tools on each machine, though some workloads require a single system with unified memory. The 512GB option remains relevant for software needing large memory pools. Apple hasn't provided official cost details for the memory upgrade.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Marvell acquires Lumentum in $115B tech deal
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: In one of the largest deals in tech history, Marvell buys Lumentum for $115B
Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion, including $35 billion in debt. Marvell will issue 4.5 shares for each Lumentum share. The transaction ranks among the largest tech acquisitions, surpassing Microsoft’s $68.7 billion Activision Blizzard purchase in 2022 and Dell’s $67 billion EMC acquisition in 2016. Both companies share Nvidia as a major shareholder, which invested $2 billion in Lumentum for R&D and fab expansion in March. Nvidia later contributed $2 billion to Marvell to strengthen its optical networking and chip capabilities. The deal positions Marvell to lead in AI connectivity, offering products from chips to data centers. The transaction is expected to close in early 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals.

item.title: Websites Block AI Agents Over Security and Control Concerns
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why some websites are blocking AI agents from accessing the web
Websites are blocking AI agents due to security and control concerns. Walmart and Amazon have restricted access, with Amazon explicitly blocking Perplexity's Comet AI tool. Meta's Muse faced CAPTCHA challenges at Walmart, which claims the verification wasn't intended for AI assistants. JPMorgan Chase cited security risks from shared credentials and screen scraping, warning customers could be liable for unauthorized actions. Amazon disputes Perplexity's claims, though a federal appeals court in August 2026 vacated a preliminary injunction against Perplexity. eBay and Delta prohibit unauthorized buy-for-me agents, while Delta denies deliberate blocking. Security systems like CAPTCHA and anti-scraping defenses often interfere with AI agents, even when legitimate. Cloudflare now distinguishes between search crawlers, AI training bots, and user agents, defaulting to blocking agents on ad pages. Shopify allows compatible agents to update orders but requires shopper authentication. Blocks aren't always intentional, as some result from automated traffic detection.

item.title: Apple's HomeView Ultra Robot to Launch in 2028 at $1,000
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Digital Trends, PCMag Original headline: Apple's HomeView Ultra Robot Set for 2028 Launch with $1,000 Price Tag
Apple is developing a high-end smart home device codenamed J595, a robotic version of its HomeView smart display. The device, potentially branded as HomeView Ultra or HomeView Max, features a 9-inch screen mounted on a swiveling robotic arm capable of following users during FaceTime calls. Hardware development has been finalized for two years, but software integration of advanced AI and home automation features is delaying the launch, expected between 2027 and 2028 at a price of around $1,000. The device would use sensors, cameras, and possibly an IR projector or Face ID setup to navigate environments, such as turning on lights when someone enters a room. The project originated in 2018 under former CEO Tim Cook, with engineers aiming to justify the high price through enhanced capabilities beyond basic video calling. The standard HomeView, a smaller 7-inch display, launched in October 2026 for $299. Critics question the market demand for a $1,000 product that primarily hosts video calls and manages lights, comparing its utility to existing smart home systems or basic robot vacuums.

item.title: Apple’s inventory jumps 154% amid rising memory costs
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Apple’s inventory surges 154% as memory chip costs climb
Apple’s inventory rose 31.1% in Q4, reaching $14.54 billion from $11.09 billion in Q3, a 154.3% year-over-year increase from $5.72 billion in Q4 2025. Higher memory chip costs drove the surge, with CEO John Ternus calling current pricing 'unprecedented.' He noted memory costs rose compared to June, partially offset by inventory carryover and lower non-memory component costs. Apple expects 'even higher memory costs' in December, which will be partially offset by price hikes on Mac, iPad, and iPhone models. Ternus warned memory costs will continue rising beyond December. COO Sabih Khan confirmed increased manufacturing purchase obligations of $33 billion since June. Supply constraints hurt iPad sales, which fell 10% year-over-year to $6.2 billion, below analyst expectations of $6.7 billion.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Smartphone users can unlock hidden features with USSD and MMI codes
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Dial These Secret Codes on Your Smartphone to Unlock Hidden Features
Smartphone users can access hidden features using USSD and MMI codes. These codes, entered into the dialer, allow direct communication with service providers to retrieve data like cell tower performance, IMEI numbers, or call forwarding settings. Examples include *#06# for IMEI, *67# to check call forwarding, and *43# to enable call waiting. Some codes, like those containing 'wipe,' can damage devices. Codes vary by carrier and device, often requiring searches for specific combinations. While useful for troubleshooting or checking balances, many codes are carrier-specific and may no longer work. Users are warned to avoid experimenting with potentially harmful commands and to note that some features, like government alerts, cannot be disabled. Carriers frequently update or deactivate these codes, making comprehensive lists impractical.

item.title: Apple Delays iPhone Duo Launch Amid Supply Chain and Memory Chip Challenges
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, The Verge Original headline: Apple Faces Prolonged iPhone Duo Delays Amid Supply Chain and Memory Chip Challenges
Apple confirmed ongoing supply constraints for its iPhone Duo, with executives acknowledging difficulty in predicting when supply and demand will balance. Chief Operating Officer Sabih Khan stated during the fiscal fourth-quarter earnings call that the ramp-up for the foldable device is progressing but noted the unpredictability of supply-demand alignment. CEO John Ternus echoed this during an interview, stating the company cannot predict balance and is working to deliver as many units as quickly as possible. Customers without preorders face delivery dates extending into 2027, with Verizon apologizing and offering gift cards. The iPhone Duo, priced at $1,999, launched with limited availability and sold out rapidly. Apple described demand as 'extraordinary,' leading to extended wait times. Supply chain struggles are tied to soaring memory chip costs driven by AI demand, with Khan noting price hikes on several products and Ternus calling current memory pricing 'unprecedented.' Apple reported record iPhone revenue of $57.58 billion in Q4, with higher prices on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models. The company is partnering with Perryman to secure titanium for the foldable device. Ternus noted a 'very small percentage' of units have been returned due to cracked screens, with replacements offered.

item.title: Apple mandates age ratings for dating and location apps
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: Apple Introduces New Age Rating Requirements for Dating and Location-Sharing Apps
Apple is requiring dating and location-sharing apps to disclose real-world location data sharing and dating features through updated App Store Connect questionnaires. Starting November 16, 2026, developers must answer these questions for all app updates and submissions by January 12, 2027. Apps with dating content will receive an 18+ rating, restricting access to users under 18 unless parental controls are disabled. Location-sharing apps face no age rating restrictions globally except in Brazil, where they must carry a 16+ rating. Developers in Brazil can request a lower rating from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security. The changes aim to address apps containing unexpected adult content, such as those initially designed for children but later found to share location data or include dating features. Parents and users will benefit from more accurate age ratings reflecting an app’s actual functionality. The updates will be integrated into App Store Connect to ensure compliance with evolving global content moderation standards.

item.title: Meta will end Quest 2 OS updates in 2027
item.description:
Source: The Verge
Meta announced it will stop providing OS updates for Quest 2 and Quest Pro headsets by March 2027. The final OS update, version 213, will be released then, after which only security patches and critical bug fixes will be available until the end of 2027. App submissions for Quest 2 and Pro will remain open until December 2027. The Quest 2 and Pro were discontinued in 2024, and Meta is shifting focus to the Quest 3 and 3S models as the new baseline for its VR ecosystem. The company plans to launch its next-generation VR Glasses in spring 2027, which will run on the same OS and SDKs as the Quest 3 and 3S. Meta stated that the Quest 2 and Pro 'laid the foundation for this platform' while emphasizing that newer devices offer improved performance and mixed reality features, with apps built for them compatible with future hardware.

item.title: Agentic AI Insights Fall Short of Business Impact
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at surveyed companies lead to business improvement. Insight leaders, a group of organizations with superior AI performance, report over 70% of insights drive business actions. Most companies struggle with prescriptive insights, citing insufficient context and fragmented data as key issues. Only 24% of organizations evaluate all agent insights, with most relying on manual, case-by-case reviews. Companies are prioritizing governance and semantic layers to enhance insight quality. Experts emphasize that without proper context, AI agents fail to deliver actionable results. The report highlights that flawed insights can cause reputational or financial harm, undermining the ROI of agentic analytics. Despite progress from 37% to 48% of effective insights in a year, over half of generated insights still lack business value. Governance and data architecture improvements are seen as critical to advancing agentic AI capabilities.

item.title: Hinge Tests Cheaper Subscription Amid User Fatigue
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Hinge tests a cheaper plan as users become more fed up paying for dating apps
Hinge is testing a cheaper subscription plan as user dissatisfaction with dating app fees grows. During Match Group’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call, the company revealed the new tier will include enhanced filters and custom location boundaries. Steve Bailey, Match Group’s CFO, noted Hinge’s pricing is nearly double Tinder’s, with lower payer penetration. The cost details remain undisclosed. Hinge’s performance outperformed Tinder, with 12% year-over-year user growth and 23% paid subscriber increase to 2.3 million. Tinder, meanwhile, saw a 2% revenue decline and 4% paid user drop. The lower-cost option aims to convert more users without higher upfront costs. This marks a shift from Hinge’s 2023 premium tier. Match Group also plans to expand Group Hangouts and real-time adaptive recommendations to combat user fatigue, aiming to make platforms feel less like traditional dating apps.

item.title: Apple Considers Third-Party AI Apps to Boost Services Revenue
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Apple may try to increase revenue by doing…something with third-party AI apps
Apple’s services business faces pressure from regulatory challenges and declining mobile gaming revenue. During an earnings call, CFO Kevan Parekh hinted at potential revenue growth through third-party apps and AI, though specifics remain unclear. Reuters speculates Apple may profit by distributing third-party AI agents via the App Store and taking a revenue cut. Regulatory changes in the U.S., Brazil, and Japan have reduced App Store commission revenue, with an 18% drop reported in the U.S. in August. A lawsuit by Epic Games forced Apple to allow external payment systems, further impacting its revenue model. Parekh noted the App Store’s performance matched the prior year’s, with record paid subscriptions, but warned of continued mobile gaming headwinds. He projected services growth of 8-9% in the December quarter, factoring in third-party licensing challenges and foreign exchange impacts. TechCrunch is awaiting Apple’s further comments on the matter.

item.title: Trajectory raises $45M to automate AI model training for non-technical users
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Trajectory raises $45M to make AI model training accessible to nontechnical experts
Trajectory, a startup founded by Stanford alumni with experience at Google DeepMind and Apple, raised $45 million in a Series A round at a $300 million valuation. The funding comes from Sequoia, Nvidia, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. The company aims to automate AI model training for specialized tasks, allowing non-technical experts to improve models through continual learning. Trajectory’s platform connects to applications to collect feedback, retraining models over time without requiring internal research teams or expensive consultants. Co-founder Ronak Malde compared foundational models to a PhD student starting a new job, emphasizing the value of experience. The startup’s approach involves human oversight, which co-founder Michael Elabd argues makes it safer than autonomous self-improvement. Customers include Harvey, Rogo, Decagon, Mercor, and Nvidia. Trajectory’s platform is now publicly available, enabling lawyers, doctors, and analysts to refine AI models for specific tasks. Competitors include Thinking Machines Lab, Applied Compute, and Prime Intellect. The team’s background in AI research and product design is cited as a key advantage.

item.title: Third US Bird Flu Death Linked to Dairy Cows
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Third person dies of bird flu since virus started jumping to livestock
A person in Washington state has died from bird flu after exposure to an infected dairy farm, marking the third human death linked to the H5 avian influenza strain since it began infecting dairy cows in the US. Health officials confirmed the death of a Yakima County resident with underlying health conditions, which likely increased their vulnerability. The individual was hospitalized and later died, though officials declined to release personal details due to privacy concerns. Dave Atteberry, Yakima Health District officer, stated the risk to the general public remains low despite the severity of the illness. Three people in Yakima County have tested positive for bird flu since October 8, all with exposure to infected dairy herds. Two of the cases involved individuals who were not hospitalized and experienced no severe symptoms.

item.title: Apple Hits iPhone Sales Record Without Standard Model
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Apple set an iPhone sales record even without a new standard iPhone
Apple reported $57.58 billion in iPhone revenue for the quarter, a 17 percent increase from the same period last year, despite not releasing a standard model. The growth followed the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, which were priced higher, alongside price hikes for older models. The iPhone Duo folding phone was also introduced but excluded from the earnings report. Apple cited higher memory costs and supply chain challenges, with CEO John Ternus noting inventory management helped offset some expenses. Overall revenue rose 12 percent to $114.5 billion. Mac sales grew 24 percent to $10.79 billion, while services revenue reached $31.57 billion. iPad sales declined 10 percent to $6.23 billion. The company expanded into smart home devices with LG and Schneider Electric partnerships and unveiled a touchscreen MacBook Pro.

item.title: AI Model Integrates RISC-V CPU for Code Execution
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: AI model gets a 32-bit RISC-V CPU compiled directly into its weights, then runs DOOM on it
AI engineer Divyansh Agrawal has developed Qwenputer, an experimental AI model that integrates a 32-bit RISC-V CPU directly into the Qwen 3.5 4B LLM's weights. The model can execute arithmetic operations, run C and MicroPython code without external tools, and operate Doom, albeit slowly. The built-in CPU provides precise calculations, addressing arithmetic limitations in many LLMs. Agrawal also added a filesystem with 1,024 slots for 512 files, using DeltaNet state for persistent storage. The model's size doubled to nearly 19GB, requiring a workstation with 24GB VRAM or more. Code for Qwenputer is available under MIT license on GitHub and via Hugging Face. The project aims to streamline coding and improve performance in future iterations.

item.title: Microsoft says Windows 11 taskbar won’t get drag-and-drop, by design
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Microsoft says Windows 11’s taskbar won’t get drag-and-drop, by design
Microsoft confirms Windows 11’s taskbar won’t support drag-and-drop repositioning, citing design choices. Users must adjust taskbar placement via the Personalization settings menu, choosing from four fixed positions: left, top, right, or bottom. The company explains this approach prevents accidental movements, a concern addressed by the 'Lock the taskbar' feature in earlier versions. Diego Baca, Microsoft’s Vice President of Design, states the decision was intentional, noting users rarely change the taskbar’s position. The feature was added five years after Windows 11’s launch in 2021, with Microsoft emphasizing a 'discoverable setting' over mouse-based drag-and-drop. While future changes aren’t ruled out, Baca asserts this remains a deliberate design choice, not a missing feature.

item.title: Squarespace lays off 19% of employees amid AI industry shifts
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Web host Squarespace lays off 19% of its employees
Squarespace, a web hosting company, is laying off approximately 19% of its workforce, affecting around 300 employees. Jeff Seedman, a public relations specialist for Squarespace, confirmed the layoffs to TechCrunch, stating the changes aim to simplify operations, sharpen priorities, and enable faster growth. The shift comes as generative AI has transformed website building, with tools like 'vibe-coding' allowing users to create sites with minimal effort. Competitors such as Wix acquired AI-driven platforms like Base44, while companies like Lovable raised $400 million in funding. Google also launched Stitch, an AI-powered design tool. Squarespace has invested in AI, launching Blueprint in 2024 and announcing Forma, an AI-native platform. Founded in 2004, the company went public in 2021 at a $10 billion valuation but struggled in public markets, leading to a $7 billion private equity deal in 2024. An earlier report incorrectly stated Squarespace had not launched AI tools, which has been corrected.

item.title: Yvonne Bajela launches $17M fund for U.K. and European startups
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Yvonne Bajela is bringing $17M in fresh capital to Europe’s startup scene
Yvonne Bajela is launching Evertrue, a $17M fund focused on early-stage AI and fintech startups in the U.K. and Europe. With a background in venture capital, she previously backed unicorns like Wise and Marshmellow. The fund will invest around £350,000 per company, targeting at least 20 startups over three years. Bajela cited the AI boom’s impact on startup economics and opportunities for early-stage investors. She noted the U.K.’s growing startup scene, including hubs like King’s Cross and companies like Revolut and Synthesia. Fundraising was challenging, with prolonged rejections costing founders time. Evertrue secured five institutional backers, including the British Business Bank and Basecamp. The fund’s size is strategic, prioritizing meaningful investments over scale. Around 80% of LPs are U.K.-based, with international backers in Asia and the U.S. Bajela emphasized backing founders with unique insights, execution ability, and ambition to build beyond initial products. She highlighted founders’ resilience and perspective shaped by their journeys, aiming for Evertrue to be known for the quality of its portfolio companies.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Phone Turns PC On Without Cost
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: I turned my phone into a power button for my PC, and it cost exactly $0
A user describes using Wake-on-LAN (WoL) to remotely power on a PC via smartphone without additional hardware. WoL sends a 'magic packet' over a network to wake a compatible PC, requiring support from the motherboard, network adapter, and BIOS/UEFI settings. A wired Ethernet connection is recommended for reliability, as Wi-Fi support is less common. Windows must also be configured to allow the network adapter to wake the computer, involving Device Manager settings and enabling 'Wake on Magic Packet.' A free phone app connects to the local network, inputs the PC's MAC address, and sends the magic packet to trigger wake-up. The method works best when the PC is in sleep mode, not a full shutdown, which may require testing. The process avoids exposing the router to the internet and leverages existing hardware for cost-effective remote PC control.

item.title: Google's Zelda Easter Egg Recreates 1998 Search Interface
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Engadget Original headline: Google's Zelda Easter Egg Transport Users Back to 1998 Search Era
Google's search interface features a Zelda-themed Easter egg for queries like 'Zelda' or 'Ocarina of Time.' A animated Master Sword appears in search results, clickable to trigger a retro-style interface with blue hyperlinks and simplified branding, evoking 1998's design. Curated results include Nintendo's Zelda page, Wikipedia, and game listings, limited to seven links. The experience lacks modern elements like AI Overviews and ads, featuring the 'I'm Feeling Lucky' button. Non-Zelda searches revert to current results, criticized as 'far worse' by Engadget. Users can switch to the Web tab for unaltered pages. The Easter egg highlights early search simplicity, contrasting with Google's current AI-driven approach. Ars Technica noted the 1998-era design mirrors the original game's debut on Nintendo 64. The feature serves as a nostalgic nod to past search mechanics, emphasizing relevance over algorithmic complexity.

item.title: Hackers claim 23TB data breach includes Ukraine war casualty figures
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Hackers claim to have stolen 23TB of data from Russian statistics body, including Ukraine war casualty figures
Hackers claim to have stolen 23TB of data from Russia's Federal State Statistics Service (Rosstat) during a cyberattack between October 29 and 31. The breach includes sensitive data marked 'for official use only,' including alleged war casualty figures from Ukraine. Rosstat denied the leak but stopped publishing annual cause-of-death statistics in 2024. Hack groups Belarusian CyberPartisans and Silent Crow claim the data shows 50,000 Russian soldiers killed monthly, with October 2026 figures near that threshold. The groups also allege wiping Rosstat's IT infrastructure, destroying systems like STATEK and StatRegister, and defacing the agency's website. Both groups are designated as extremists in Russia. They previously claimed responsibility for hacks targeting Aeroflot and a state real estate company in 2025. Rosstat remains inaccessible as the incident develops.

item.title: Garry Tan spends $200K annually on AI tokens
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Y Combinator’s Garry Tan uses AI agents so much, he spends up to $200K a year on tokens
Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan spends $100,000 to $200,000 annually on AI tokens for personal and professional tasks. He uses AI agents to manage email, Dropbox, Apple Notes, and therapy records, describing them as constant assistants that anticipate needs. Tan shared his 23 Claude Code skills toolkit, gstack, on GitHub to demonstrate agent capabilities. Y Combinator employs an internal AI agent named Stray Light, which maintains context about founders and applicants. Tan argues AI agents should not be treated like traditional software, emphasizing their human-like adaptability. He acknowledges high costs as a barrier to mainstream adoption, noting his spending represents a privilege. Tan criticizes Big Tech's control over AI algorithms, advocating for user-controlled personal agents. He envisions a future where affordable, customizable AI tools become standard.

item.title: Voyager 1 regains contact after communication blackout
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Voyager 1 Is Approaching a Full Light-Day From Earth—and It Just Scared the Crap Out of NASA
NASA’s Voyager 1 briefly lost contact with Earth in mid-October after its radio signal failed to detect during two communication attempts. The signal resumed on October 20, with engineers determining a group of thrusters went offline, triggering backup systems. Mission manager Kareem Badaruddin noted the spacecraft’s automatic response places it in a stable configuration for investigation. Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is expected to reach one light-day from Earth on November 18, a distance of 16.09 billion miles. NASA recently performed a power-saving maneuver, switching off three devices for lower-power alternatives, extending the probe’s operational life beyond 2027. The twin Voyager probes, powered by decaying plutonium, lose 4 watts annually. Voyager 1 continues collecting data in interstellar space, with no environmental changes expected as it approaches the milestone. Project manager Suzanne Dodd explained communication delays will take 24 hours for messages to reach the spacecraft.

item.title: Xiaomi to Launch 18 Pro Series Globally in November
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Xiaomi's going global—the 18 Pro series is preparing for a major November launch
Xiaomi confirmed the global launch of its 18 Pro series in November, though an exact date remains unspecified. The series, which debuted in China in September, has generated anticipation for its international rollout. Rumors suggest global pricing starts at €1,449 (~$1,622) for the 12GB/256GB model, with higher tiers reaching €1,849 (~$2,070). Battery capacities may also decrease, with the Pro model potentially dropping to 6,000mAh and the Pro Max to 7,050mAh compared to Chinese versions. The phones feature location-based privacy displays that hide sensitive data from alerts, along with upgraded rear displays integrating Xiao AI functions. Xiaomi's president emphasized retaining rear displays, following the successful 17 series launch. The 18 Pro series introduces enhanced privacy features, including automatic hiding of banking notifications and floating windows, surpassing Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra capabilities.

item.title: Google Tests Android-Style Status Bar for Wear OS 8
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google's Wear OS 'status bar' experiment brings a little more Android flair to watches
Google is testing a status bar for Wear OS 8, mirroring Android's design. The status bar will appear at the 12 o'clock position on smartwatches, displaying time and status icons like connectivity and location. This change aims to provide visual consistency across apps and ensure a uniform clock typography. Developers are preparing for the update via Android Studio Preview. The status bar will temporarily hide during scrolling and reappear afterward. Earlier this year, Google expanded earthquake alerts to Wear OS, allowing standalone notifications without a paired phone. Wear OS 7, released in June, introduced improved battery life and enhanced device integration, enabling media control across devices and audio transfer. Gemini Intelligence and 'Create My Widget' features were also part of Wear OS 7 updates for select models.

item.title: iPhone call decline options depend on device state and settings
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The reason why some iPhone calls don't have a decline option, and others do
iPhone call decline options depend on device state and settings. When locked, incoming calls show a 'slide to answer' control, while unlocked devices display answer or decline buttons. Settings adjust button placement but not availability. Users can decline calls by pressing the side button twice or volume buttons, sending callers to voicemail. A 'Message' option allows sending text replies via the incoming call interface, with customizable responses. Blocking unwanted numbers via the 'Recents' list or 'Screen Unknown Callers' setting helps manage spam. The Federal Trade Commission reported over 2.6 million Do Not Call complaints in fiscal year 2025. Unknown callers can be silenced or prompted for identification, though caution is advised to avoid blocking legitimate contacts.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: iPhone Messages App Allows Customization for Better Organization
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: One annoying problem with the iPhone Messages app has an easy fix
Apple's iMessage app allows users to customize its dropdown menu for better organization. By default, iOS 27 includes 14 apps like location sharing, polls, and Venmo, expanding messaging features. Users can rearrange apps by holding and dragging them within the Messages app. Additional apps can be added via the App Store within iMessage, though some require purchases. Privacy concerns arose in 2026 when OpenAI's ChatGPT app integrated with iMessage, sparking debates over security. Family Sharing plans offer parental controls to manage in-app purchases, including the 'Ask To Buy' feature. To remove apps, users can delete them through Settings or the device's home screen. Customization also extends to audio recording functions within iMessage, allowing toggling between voice notes and dictation.

item.title: Nagoshi Studio Closes After Gang of Dragon Development Halted
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Nagoshi Studio, from the creator of the Yakuza series, officially shuts down
Nagoshi Studio, founded by Yakuza creator Toshihiro Nagoshi, has officially closed after less than a year of operations. The studio announced its dissolution on October 31 via Japan's official gazette, citing the end of its shareholders meeting. The studio had been developing Gang of Dragon, a game set in Tokyo's Kabuchiko district with a new protagonist, Shin Ji-Seong. Despite a December 2025 trailer showcasing the project, NetEase withdrew funding, leaving over $44 million needed to complete the game. With the studio now liquidating assets and resolving liabilities, Gang of Dragon's Steam page remains active but its release prospects are uncertain. The closure marks the end of Nagoshi's post-Yakuza ventures.

item.title: Affinity’s all-in-one creative app is finally here for iPad, and it costs nothing
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends
Affinity released its all-in-one creative app for iPad, nearly a year after launching on Mac and Windows. The free version includes core tools like Sketch, Vector, Pixel, and Layout, with additional features for Apple Pencil and touchscreen. New tools include Sketch Studio for drawing with pressure and tilt controls, Sketch to Shapes for converting hand-drawn shapes into editable vectors, and Mask Tool for selecting complex edges. AI Studio adds Generative Expand, image upscaling, and Decompose Layer for splitting flattened images into editable layers. Advanced Apple Pencil Pro features like barrel roll and squeeze are also available. AI-powered tools require a premium Canva account, while core tools are free for individuals. The app is now on the iPad App Store, needing a free Canva account to access.

item.title: Samsung Rumored to Launch Intelligent Eyewear Near Christmas 2026
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Samsung's 'Intelligent Eyewear' is now rumored to launch near Christmas
Samsung's Intelligent Eyewear, its Android XR glasses, is rumored to launch in mid-December 2026 in South Korea and the U.S. The company plans to monitor initial demand and user reactions in these markets before expanding globally. Pricing remains uncertain, with reports suggesting a 'reasonable' price above Meta's $300 Ray-Bans. The glasses will connect to compatible Galaxy Watches for gesture control and photo capture. Design collaborations with Warby Parker and Gentle Monster are highlighted. Earlier rumors had placed the launch in November, but the latest speculation shifts to December. Samsung is still evaluating final pricing details ahead of the December release. The product is positioned as an extension of Galaxy phones, not a standalone device.

item.title: Wearables Predict Blood Pressure Crises Days in Advance
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The wearable on your wrist can predict blood pressure crisis events days in advance
Wearable devices can predict episodes of dangerously high blood pressure, or hypertensive crisis, up to three days in advance, according to a study by the American Heart Association. The research involved 4,000 participants with stage 2 hypertension who wore a portable blood pressure monitor and a fitness tracker. Data from both devices, analyzed by an AI model, identified risk patterns, enabling early warnings. Among participants, 312 experienced hypertensive crises, with those receiving alerts and timely medication seeing a 61% reduction in crisis risk and a 45% drop in emergency hospital visits. The study found that individuals whose blood pressure did not decrease during sleep had five times higher crisis risk. While wearables like Apple Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch track heart rate and HRV, they cannot measure specific systolic and diastolic values like medical-grade devices. Huawei’s Watch D3, however, uses a micropump cuff for accurate blood pressure readings. Experts note wearables are advancing but remain early warning tools, not replacements for medical equipment.

item.title: iPadOS 27.2 Simplifies Split View Inspired by iPhone Duo's Multitasking
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The iPhone Duo taught the iPad a much-needed lesson in multitasking. iPadOS 27.2 makes Split View less of a chore.
iPadOS 27.2 simplifies Split View multitasking by making side-by-side app setup easier. Previously, users had to manually resize and switch apps, but the update now automatically places a second app beside the first with a single tap after tiling. The change is inspired by the iPhone Duo’s intuitive multitasking interface, which Apple has adapted for the iPad. While not identical, the new system is closer to the foldable iPhone’s approach. Apple is also testing iOS 27.2.1 for bug fixes and potential iPhone Duo improvements, with a public release expected in December 2026. A beta for iOS 27.3, featuring Apple Intelligence in China on iPhone 15 Pro models, is set for November 3, 2026, though iPad support is pending.

item.title: Airport USB Charging Risks Exist, But Safeguards Available
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Is it actually safe to charge your iPhone at airport USB ports?
US agencies like the FBI and TSA warn against charging iPhones at airport USB ports due to 'juice-jacking' risks, but security experts say the threat is overblown. The TSA advised in March 2025 against using public USB ports, recommending TSA-compliant power bricks. The FCC initially warned about 'port-jacking' attacks but later retracted the warning after experts disputed its validity. Security researchers note while USB standards allow data and power transfer, proof-of-concept attacks like the 2013 Mactans charger prototype demonstrate potential risks. Apple addressed the issue by adding a 'Trust This Computer?' prompt in iOS updates. No credible reports of successful attacks exist. To mitigate risks, users should avoid public USB ports, use personal chargers, or employ USB data blockers. Secure charging stations and avoiding public Wi-Fi with multi-factor authentication are also recommended. The TSA and others advise carrying backup power sources for safety.

item.title: China outlines 2030 lunar landing plan with detailed mission timeline
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: China publicly discloses plan for a lunar landing within three years
Chinese space officials announced plans to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030. At the Seventh Manned Spaceflight Conference, Wang Xiang, chief designer for the lunar exploration program, outlined a series of missions. The plan includes uncrewed tests of the Long March 10A rocket and Mengzhou spacecraft in 2027, followed by uncrewed lunar lander tests in 2028. In 2029, two Long March 10 rockets will launch concurrently, docking in lunar orbit. A crewed mission targeting before 2030 will follow. The approach uses a lunar-orbit rendezvous, similar to Apollo but with separate launches due to less powerful rockets. The plan excludes Apollo 8-like missions but includes Earth-orbit tests for the Mengzhou vehicle. NASA aims for a 2028 lunar landing, while the U.S. has been developing the Space Launch System and Orion spacecraft for over a decade. China’s timeline positions it to potentially reach the Moon ahead of the U.S. by a year.

item.title: Lego's Largest Set, Sagrada Família, Released in November
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: The Largest Lego Set Ever Is Among November’s Releases
Lego's largest set ever, the Sagrada Família cathedral, is among November's releases. The 12,000-piece set, priced at $800, is available now. It features intricate details of the Barcelona landmark. Also released is a Dragon Ball set depicting Shenron and Goku for $180, available November 4. A Venice-themed set includes 17 mini-figures, priced at $550, and is also available November 4. A smaller, more affordable set at $23 is highlighted for its versatility as a gift. The Sagrada Família set breaks the previous record of 11,695 pieces. Lego's November lineup includes fewer new releases compared to usual, but the Sagrada Família and other sets receive special attention for their scale and detail.

item.title: UN Nations Agree to Boost Biodiversity Efforts Despite Funding Gaps
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: The world has a new plan to save nature, but it still needs the money
UN nations missed 2030 conservation targets as finance and action lagged, according to leaders at the COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan. Over two weeks, representatives from nearly 200 countries reviewed progress on the 2022 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, which aimed to protect a third of the world’s land and seas by 2030. The summit concluded with agreement on the Yerevan Pathway, a plan to accelerate efforts before the next summit in Ecuador. Key measures include reforming harmful subsidies, increasing financial support for developing nations, and improving monitoring. Steven Guilbeault, former Canadian environment minister, called finance the biggest barrier, citing an underfunded voluntary genetic materials fund. He urged more public and private investment, better subsidy reforms, and ensuring funds reach frontline communities. The summit acknowledged slow progress but committed to intensified action despite persistent funding gaps.

item.title: Never plug power strips into each other to avoid fire risks
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Why it's important to never plug power strips into each other
Daisy-chaining power strips can overload circuits and cause fires. Each strip's maximum amp rating limits electrical capacity, and connecting multiple strips forces the first to carry combined loads, risking overheating and resistive heating. This can melt insulation and ignite flammable materials. High-power devices like space heaters, microwaves, and refrigerators should not be plugged into power strips. Solutions include using longer cords, separate strips with proper ratings, or additional wall outlets. Surge protectors do not increase capacity and should not be daisy-chained. Always check device and strip ratings to avoid overloading. Damaged or overloaded strips require immediate attention, as they pose significant fire hazards.

item.title: Lexar launches world’s thinnest portable SSD, Muse
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: [EXCLUSIVE]: How Lexar made Muse, the world’s thinnest portable SSD that looks like a metal card
Lexar, a storage company known for memory cards and drives, launched Muse, the world’s thinnest portable SSD, at IFA 2026. The device, resembling a metal card, measures 1 mm in thickness and attaches magnetically to smartphones. Lexar addressed thermal concerns by using a single-sided PCB layout, low-power NAND, and an all-metal chassis to dissipate heat away from the phone. The drive maintains peak performance during high-bitrate video recording without thermal throttling. Stability of the PogoPin connection was ensured through gold-plated contacts and precision magnetic alignment. Durability tests included 10,000 mating cycles, salt-spray exposure, and resistance to contaminants. Muse is available in 512GB and 1TB variants, with a 2TB model under validation. Lexar emphasized that the ultra-thin design relies on optimized components and packaging, not a single technique, allowing it to bypass conventional size constraints of portable SSDs.
